title: Make TemperSwift Windows toolchain downloads production-safe
description: TemperSwift used the Swift website API identifier `win10` as the download.swift.org directory, producing a false 404. The canonical artifact directory is `windows10`. After correcting that distinction, the 1.72 GiB main-snapshot installer resolves with HTTP 200, but the Windows OpenAPI URLSession streaming transport crashes in FoundationNetworking while beginning the transfer. AsyncHTTPClient is not a Windows fallback because its CAsyncHTTPClient shim requires Unix strptime APIs. Complete this production fix by adding a bounded file-download capability to the Windows wrkstrm-networking backend and consuming that capability from TemperSwift without loading the installer into memory.
acceptanceCriteria: TemperSwift preserves `win10` for Swift website metadata lookup and uses `windows10` for toolchain artifact directory URLs.
Swift Testing covers the Windows identifier distinction and a non-Windows control platform.
The Windows download path streams a multi-gigabyte artifact directly to a destination file through the canonical wrkstrm-networking Windows backend, with bounded memory and progress reporting.
HTTP status, redirect, cancellation, partial-file cleanup, and disk-write failures become typed errors instead of crashes.
Temper installs, verifies, and selects a current main-snapshot toolchain on Windows through the production CLI.
The implementation does not patch SwiftPM checkouts and does not enable AsyncHTTPClient on Windows while its Unix C shim remains incompatible.
